rules.name: Unexpected member of a monitored privileged local group
rules.description: A member of a monitored local group (default: Administrators) is not on the expectedPrivilegedMembers allowlist.
rules.rationale: Unexpected administrators can come from account creation or group changes by an intruder, but also from normal provisioning. The rule compares current state to an allowlist; it cannot show who made the change or when.
rules.titleTemplate: {MemberName} is a member of {Group} but is not on the allowlist
falsePositives: Domain or helpdesk groups added by policy that are missing from the allowlist
rules.recommendedNextStep: Check Security events 4720 (account created) and 4732 (member added) for the account, confirm with the owner, and review its logon history.
rules.remediation: If the membership is not approved, an authorized administrator could remove it after the account has been investigated. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: This is a state check without a change event, so it has no ATT&CK mapping; WTH-EVT-005 maps the observed change event.

rules.name: Built-in Guest account is enabled
rules.description: The built-in Guest account (RID 501) is enabled.
rules.rationale: The Guest account is disabled by default. Enabling it allows anonymous-style local access and is rarely intentional.
rules.titleTemplate: The built-in Guest account is enabled
falsePositives: Kiosk or lab machines configured to allow guest access
rules.recommendedNextStep: Find out who enabled the account and when (Security 4722), and check for logons by the account.
rules.remediation: An authorized administrator could disable the account if guest access is not required. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: An enabled Guest account is a weak configuration, not a technique, so this rule has no ATT&CK mapping.

rules.name: Enabled local account does not require a password
rules.description: An enabled local account other than Guest has the PasswordRequired flag cleared.
rules.rationale: Accounts that do not need a password are easier to abuse, particularly for remote or scheduled use.
rules.titleTemplate: Enabled account {AccountName} does not require a password
falsePositives: Service or lab accounts created without a password policy
rules.recommendedNextStep: Review how and when the account was created and whether it has logged on interactively or over the network.
rules.remediation: An authorized administrator could require a password or disable the account after confirming it is not needed. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: A weak account setting is not a technique, so this rule has no ATT&CK mapping.
